source.title: [PDF] ASSESSMENT OF TOTALENERGIES' CLIMATE STRATEGY
source.snippet: To assess TotalEnergies’ climate strategy and provide our analysis, Reclaim Finance relied on the International Energy Agency’s (IEA) Net Zero Emissions by 2050 Scenario (NZE).1 The NZE is based on a 1.5°C trajectory and includes: • A drop in oil and gas production of 21% and 18% respectively by 2030, compared with 2022 levels. Indeed, during this period, the company fully acquired Total Eren in 2023 (3.5 GW),40 acquired 50% of ClearWay in the United States in 2022 (3.9 GW),41 20% of Adani Green in 2021 (3 GW) and 50% of Adani Green’s solar assets in 2020 (2.3 GW).42 As TotalEnergies is developing new oil and gas upstream and LNG projects, additional renewable capacities do not change the company’s fossil-based business model.43 If TotalEnergies meets its targets, the maximum renewable power energy share of the company’s energy production mix in 2030 would remain under 10%, while oil and gas extraction will represent 82% of its energy production mix.
